study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Di Biase et al., Molecular Psychiatry, 2022
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Three datasets were used: (1) Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample (HCP-1200), (2) Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCP-Psychosis), and (3) Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB). HCP-YA and HCP-EP were combined to form the discovery cohort; ASRB was used as the validation cohort.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: This study comprised a total of 1849 participants drawn from three independent datasets: (1) the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample [15]; (2) the Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCPpsychosis) [16]; and (3) the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB) [17].

answer.HCP-YA: normative model training (discovery cohort) - healthy controls

answer.HCP-EP: normative model training (discovery cohort) - healthy controls and cases for validation

answer.ASRB: normative model validation and genomic validation of cell-based patient subtypes

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: HCP-YA (HCP-1200) and HCP-EP (HCP-Psychosis) were combined to form the discovery cohort (n=1267 comprising 140 cases and 1127 controls). The normative model was trained on healthy controls from this combined dataset. ASRB was used as the validation cohort (n=520 comprising 335 cases and 185 controls) to evaluate replicability and validity, and for genomic validation of cell-based patient subtypes.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: The HCP-Young Adult Sample and HCP-psychosis datasets were acquired using very similar MRI protocols (see Supplementary Material), enabling them to be combined to form a single discovery cohort (n = 1267 comprising 140 cases ... and 1127 controls ...). The ASRB dataset was used to evaluate replicability and validity (n = 520 comprising 335 cases ... and 185 controls ...).

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study established separate normative models for discovery (HCP) and validation (ASRB) cohorts. For the HCP discovery cohort, 1127 healthy controls (62 from HCP-Psychosis + 1065 from HCP-1200) were used to establish normative ranges. For the ASRB validation cohort, 185 healthy controls were used. The paper does not explicitly distinguish between train and test phases within each normative model.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: To characterize CTh heterogeneity, normative ranges of variation in each brain region were established based on healthy individuals (n = 1127 for HCP [discovery] and n = 185 for ASRB [validation])

Supplementary Table 1 shows: HCP-1200 HC (n=1065): 28.75 +/- 3.67; HCP-Psychosis HC (n=62): 24.30 +/- 4.10. For ASRB validation cohort healthy controls: age 41.05 +/- 14.02 years (n=185). Age range (min/max) was not explicitly reported.
